speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you have chronic pain in your left shoulder without a history of trauma. To begin our assessment, has this pain been present for more than three months, and does it worsen at night or when lying on that side?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old woman. The patient reports a 2-month history of insidious onset left shoulder pain, worsening with extreme ranges of motion and activity. Pain disrupts sleep, and there's noted difficulty with activities of daily living like brushing hair and dressing. No history of shoulder trauma, neck pain, arm/hand weakness, numbness, or paresthesias. The patient has type 2 diabetes mellitus, treated with metformin and glipizide.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Rotator Cuff Tendinopathy (likely Supraspinatus)

Based on your 2-month history of pain worsening with motion and at night, I need to assess your specific range of motion limitations. Please try to raise your left arm straight up in front of you; how high can you get before the pain stops you? Also, does bringing your arm across your body to touch the opposite shoulder cause sharp pain?
